Bulk and cascade mutation (retiring a statement and everything transitively dependent on it) is deliberately not specified; the atomicity mode is declared but transitive closure belongs to the structural and traversal areas.

Reconciliation of competing evidence - how a human declaration and a contradicting observation are resolved into one current assertion - is left as a declared precedence rule without a merge algorithm.
Late-arriving and out-of-order observations are surfaced as a question and an adversarial check, but no default ordering discipline is prescribed.
Schema evolution of the statement payload itself (migrating stored historical versions across structural changes) is governed by the structural area's compatibility rules, not here.
No quantitative service expectations (throughput, replay-window defaults, retention periods) are asserted; these are adopting-Dimension parameters.
conflicts: Client-supplied idempotency keys are widespread practice but have no stable normative basis: the IETF draft that would standardize the header expired at revision 07 without becoming an RFC. The model therefore treats the key as a local contract parameter and takes its binding guarantees from RFC 9110 idempotency and conditional requests instead.

Version-conflict signalling is not uniform: FHIR permits both 409 Conflict and 412 Precondition Failed for the same class of failure, so any interface binding must choose one and declare it; the model keeps stale-version and illegal-transition as distinct semantic outcomes regardless of the chosen status code.

SPDX models a relationship as an asserted element with creation metadata but has no state machine, no approval gate and no supersession semantics. The lifecycle defined here is an addition layered on top of that vocabulary, not SPDX conformance, and round-tripping loses the workflow states.

PROV-O's wasRevisionOf does not distinguish a correction of an erroneous record from a legitimate revision. The distinction is imported from a clinical status vocabulary (amended, corrected, entered-in-error) and is therefore not interoperable by default; exporters must carry the change-nature code explicitly.

CloudEvents allows a producer to set the time attribute either to the actual occurrence time or by a consistent algorithm, so the envelope alone cannot carry the event-time versus ingestion-time distinction; both times must travel in the event data, not only in the envelope.

The publication-status vocabulary treats retired as covering both withdrawn and superseded, whereas this model separates retirement from supersession because they assert different things about currency; mapping to that vocabulary is therefore lossy in one direction.
regional_assumptions: No jurisdiction-specific electronic-records regime is assumed. Where one applies (for example a validated-systems or records-integrity regime), the adopting Dimension's audit and retention models must add signature manifestation, signature-to-record linking and audit-trail retention obligations; this model provides the hooks but asserts none of them.

Approval expectations, including whether separation of duties is mandatory, vary by sector and regulator; four-eyes is modelled as a configurable constraint with an explicit violation outcome rather than as a default.

All times are recorded with explicit offsets; local civil-time rules, daylight-saving transitions and non-Gregorian calendars are outside the model, and '-00:00' is reserved for a genuinely unknown local offset.
Data-residency and cross-border constraints on where command, approval and observation records may be stored are storage-projection concerns owned by the adopting Dimension, not by these semantics.
adversarial_checks: Replay the same declare command twice with the same idempotency key but different payloads: the contract must refuse the second on fingerprint mismatch with no partial effect, rather than creating a second statement or silently overwriting the first.

Issue an approve command whose authorization decision reference resolves to Deny, Indeterminate or nothing at all: admission must fail closed in all three cases; a design that treats a missing decision as permissive is a boundary violation.

Issue a correct command against a version that has already been superseded: history must afterwards show the corrected version, the entered-in-error marker, and the intact supersession chain, and the correction must not resurrect the superseded statement as current.

Submit an observation-update whose phenomenon time precedes the phenomenon time already recorded: the contract must classify it as late-arriving evidence or refuse it as out of order, and must never silently overwrite the more recent observation.
Retire a statement whose target endpoint reference no longer resolves: retirement must succeed on the local statement while making no attempt to create, modify or delete the endpoint record.

Grep every function, effect and artifact in this model for policy evaluation, access enforcement, audit-record writing, package resolution, deployment or notification delivery: any hit indicates ownership of a target model's semantics and must be moved to a composition link or an out-of-scope entry.

Attempt an atomic multi-statement revision in which one statement's version precondition is stale: either all statements are left unchanged or the declared per-statement mode is honoured with an explicit per-statement outcome list - a silent partial application falsifies the atomicity claim.

Re-import an exported history after a contract major-version upgrade: statement identifiers, version tokens and event identifiers must resolve unchanged, proving that upgrading the contract never rewrites history.
